review.evidence: Judged by visual event, not title: c1's event is a flat monochrome contour silhouette painted on the backdrop wall with the real bottle optically 'filling' its lower portion from a fixed eye-level view (shape-recognition alignment, a graphic double on a vertical plane); c2's event is arrival trace on a horizontal tabletop - condensation mist, water rings and a damp shadow zone around the base while the cutout's own droplets stay untouched (contact/temperature narrative); c3's event is a single elongated contour-profiled cast shadow stretching across the floor toward the viewer, implying travel the static bottle never makes (shadow-as-precursor on a horizontal plane, physically distinct from c1's wall graphic); c4's event is concentric tonal ripple bands in floor and backdrop gradient converging on the base, i.e.环境 geometry organised by the red band and cap (chromatic gravity, no silhouette double at all). Product integrity holds in all four: container, crown cap, red label band, white script, amber liquid and observed droplets are preserved; moisture in c2 exists only on the generated surface, never repainted onto the cutout; c3's shadow is a diffuse floor cast/contact shadow consistent with the observed soft front/above studio light, not a relight; c1 and c4 add only generated scenery. No flavour, ingredient, nutrition, price, history or new-product claims appear; copy stays within ORIGINAL TASTE plus authored Chinese lines. Differences are mechanism-level (wall silhouette alignment vs surface trace vs floor shadow path vs concentric colour field), not mere resizes, repositionings, palette swaps or renamed materials, so no group collapses into a single isolated packshot.
review.required_revision: No merge required; tighten execution guards instead. c1: state that the wall silhouette is cropped by the set's top edge as intended scenery and verify the real bottle's alignment reads at poster distance without touching the cutout. c2: keep surface moisture coherent - rings and mist must radiate plausibly from the base contact point and never appear on the glass. c3: render the elongated shadow strictly as a soft diffuse cast/contact shadow under the existing soft front/above light; forbid hard directional relighting or a second shadow. c4: keep concentric tonal bands low-contrast so the grey void never competes with the red band, and confirm no gradient overlaps or clips the label. Preserve all four concepts as separate executions.
